text: Advanced effects are still effects: tasks, shared state, observation, time, and control flow of your own.
Each one is answered by a handler. Stack the handlers, and they work on one program together.
Three tasks share one counter. The state handler sits outside the scheduler, so every task reads and writes the same store.
A task runs until it waits. A Get and its Put, with no wait between them, are never split. A hundred each makes three hundred.
Wait between the Get and the Put, and the other tasks read the same old value. Two of every three updates are lost: one hundred.
Hold a semaphore of one across the read and the write, and the count is three hundred again.
WithObserve shows you every effect that part of a program yields, without handling any of them.
It sees the effects of tasks spawned inside its scope, and nothing yielded outside it.
Each effect still goes on to its handler. The result and the log are the same as without the observer.
Control flow of your own is a handler for an effect of your own. Audit and Abort are plain data classes.
The Audit handler resumes k, so checkout goes on after the Audit.
The Abort handler never resumes k. The body ends right where it yielded Abort, and the handler's value is the result.
With stock, checkout returns ordered. Without, the result is: aborted, out of stock.
Time is effects too. Delay and GetTime mean what the time handler says.
Under the sync handler, a one and a half second Delay sleeps for real. Under the simulated clock, the clock moves, and the run takes under a millisecond, even for an hour.
doeff: tasks, state, observation, time and your own control flow are all effects, and the handlers you stack decide what each one does. pip install doeff.
